brief: Two bases a cell apart, with a drawer that fills the gap between them.

requirements.requirement: Two bases a cell apart (one empty cell position between them)
requirements.evidence: There are two full bases, piece:0,0,0 and piece:1,0,0, but they sit next to each other and are joined by jointBolt:0#0,0#0. I first tried them with an empty cell between them (0,0 and 2,0), but no drawer could fit there (see below), so I moved them together.

requirements.requirement: A drawer that fills the gap between them
requirements.evidence: notch:0#1,-1#notch4 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) fills the empty position at (1,-1), which touches both bases. It is not in a straight gap between two bases that are apart. With the bases at 0,0 and 2,0, every addNotch at 1,0 (both hands, k 0 to 5) was refused with NO_CELL or HAND_MISMATCH, and find_sockets offered no notch spots. The notch drawer only fits in the V-shaped gap beside two touching bases. The bay drawer needs three bases.
check_build: ok, meshClash clear, no errors (info only: 8 open faces could take caps).

finish.summary: A drawer in a straight gap between two separated bases isn't possible: the notch drawer has to bolt to two bases that touch each other. Closest supported build: two touching full bases joined by a joint bolt, with a notch drawer frame filling the V-shaped gap beside both. Checks pass and the meshes are clear.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
